title: Model and Effort in Chat

sources.text: Plan a change in the chat input where we change the model and effort selection to look like Image 1
Rounded dark card; lightning glyph; centered blue High above GPT-6.1 Sol and chevron; reset arrow; blue and neutral discrete slider with white thumb and tick dots.

src/views/codex_view.rs option_triggers, open_menu, menu_choices, effective_model and choose_option; crates/grove-core/src/codex.rs and claude.rs Configure and ResetConfiguration; DESIGN.md and grove-ui skill.

claims.text: One compact control groups model and effort above the composer.

nodes.text: Reference hierarchy · not a pixel rendering

decisions.prompt: How should this card appear in the chat input?

options.label: Combined trigger and popover (Recommended)
options.description: Replace model and effort toolbar controls with one compact summary; open the card above it on click or keyboard activation.

options.label: Always visible card
options.description: Keep the card in the composer toolbar area; consumes more vertical space at narrow widths.

children.text: The card retains its hierarchy at narrow widths.

exhibit.text:
Upper row: decorative lightning, centered effort and model, trailing reset.
Lower row: rounded track, blue completed portion, neutral remainder, tick dots, contrasting round thumb.
Long model names truncate with full accessible label. Keep the card within the window and anchor it above the composer.
Use token dimensions, theme colors, shared control shells and icon assets. Neutral focus fills keep borders stable; buttons return to rest on release.
Light appearance follows the fixed app palette. White thumb in dark mode maps to an appropriate contrasting semantic treatment in light mode.

children.text: The combined control preserves the existing access control.

entries.title: Combine toolbar entries
entries.detail: Replace model and effort entries; retain access as its existing separate control.

entries.title: Anchor the card
entries.detail: Extend menu state and rendering, keeping current outside-click dismissal behavior.

entries.title: Place the overlay
entries.detail: Reuse the composer overlay path for a reference-shaped card.

claims.text: The slider selects only efforts supported by the current model.

exhibit.text:
0 supported efforts → unavailable/default explanation, no invented stops.
1 supported effort → fixed labeled value, no draggable illusion.
N supported efforts → ordered catalog stops; readable current effort above the track.
Click snaps to a supported stop. Drag previews locally; pointer release commits once.
Arrow keys change one stop; Home/End choose endpoints. Announce current effort and range through accessible semantics.
Model row opens the existing model choices within the same anchored surface.
Model change recomputes stops and reconciles effort through each provider’s existing default behavior. Never carry an unsupported effort into a new model.

children.text: Effort membership follows the effective model, including resolved Claude models.

entries.title: Read model capabilities
entries.detail: Derive ordered supportedReasoningEfforts from the selected effective catalog entry.

entries.title: Resolve provider aliases
entries.detail: Preserve existing effective_model handling and Claude resolved-catalog regression coverage.

entries.title: Dispatch supported values
entries.detail: Reuse Configure from choose_option; catalog-gate slider values because core enum validation alone does not validate per-model membership.

claims.text: Selection changes the next turn without submitting the chat draft.

screen.text: Combined summary and separate access control in the toolbar.
Effort, model row, reset, discrete slider. Focus enters the control.
Existing catalog labels and selected model; return to the effort card after selection.
Thumb and effort label preview a supported stop. No provider write until release.

transitions.label: Release commits supported effort; cancel discards preview
Escape returns focus to model row

children.text: Dismissal restores focus without changing another session.

exhibit.text:
Escape from the card returns focus to the trigger. Outside click keeps the clicked destination’s focus.
Session/provider switch dismisses both levels and cancels pointer preview; stale callbacks must never configure the new session.
Keyboard navigation, focus-visible styling and accessible control names remain usable.
Selection dispatches Configure for the originating session, preserves draft and attachments, and does not send a prompt.

claims.text: Reset restores configured model and effort independently of access.

exhibit.text:
Recommended reset scope: clear model and effort overrides, restore configured/resolved model and effort, preserve access override and persisted access.
Current ResetConfiguration clears all three fields in both actors; it cannot be reused unchanged for this arrow.
Introduce a narrowly scoped action or explicit reset scope handled by both providers. Preserve existing all-settings reset behavior elsewhere.
Codex must reconcile configured-turn state and persistence; Claude must reconfigure without losing saved access.
Do not implement reset by guessing defaults or sending empty Configure fields.

decisions.prompt: What should the card’s reset arrow reset?

options.label: Model and effort only (Recommended)
options.description: Restore their configured values while keeping the separate access setting unchanged.

options.label: All composer settings
options.description: Reuse the existing reset, including access; the control must clearly disclose this wider effect.

children.text: Both providers persist the selected reset scope consistently.

entries.title: Codex reset and configure
entries.detail: Add scoped clearing beside ResetConfiguration; retain configured-turn resolved values and access override. Model change already selects the new catalog default effort.

entries.title: Claude reset and configure
entries.detail: Add equivalent scoped clearing and reconfiguration; preserve saved access. Existing model changes clear effort.

claims.text: Both providers must pass interaction, persistence and visual acceptance checks.

exhibit.text:
Implementation checks: relevant cargo test core/view regression cases and full cargo test conformance. Orchestrator reads raw results independently.
Regression cases: catalog 0/1/N stops; supported-only writes; aliases/resolved models; model change defaults; drag cancel/commit; session switch; reset plus unchanged access and persistence.
Native QA: actual build/worktree identified; dark/light, desktop/narrow composer, long model names, resting/hover/focus/open/release states, keyboard and pointer use, model switch, dismissal and reset. Compare against Image 1 and this contract.
Codex live boundary: currently UNTESTED (plan only). Later verify next-turn effective model/effort and scoped reset/access against real provider state.
Claude live boundary: currently UNTESTED (plan only). Later verify resolved catalog, next-turn settings and scoped reset/access against real provider state.
Report Codex and Claude separately as verified, unsupported or untested, naming actual method or blocker. Fixtures establish local logic only, never live provider behavior.
Cover affected supported platforms; explicitly mark native or platform checks not exercised. No build/install occurs during this plan.

scope: Plan only: no application code, builds, tests or installation are performed for this proposal. File counts estimate implementation changes, excluding plan artifacts.
Apply to the shared Codex and Claude chat composer. Access stays separate. Preserve drafts, attachments, sending and provider catalog discovery.
The lightning is decorative; do not invent a speed or billing control. Effort stop counts follow each model’s catalog, rather than copying the reference dots literally.

Blue effort text and slider fill follow the explicit reference. Document this focused exception in DESIGN.md; use existing semantic colors, tokens, shared controls and icons. No arbitrary palette, scale expansion or conformance allow-list.

Review response resolves proposal decisions. Implementation needs a later explicit request. After authorized implementation: relevant checks and native QA, then ./install.sh once at the selected final delivery endpoint unless subsequently deferred.
